You have our deepest apologies
and enormous thanks. Take off the wig,
441:
wash off the tattoos, go home
and celebrate New Year. Thank you very much.
- What about my men?
442:
We'll take your charges back
to prison today.
443:
If you find the cloakroom attendant,
might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you, but Bely,
the real Docent, escaped today.
445:
Unbelievable, but true. It's dangerous
for you to keep looking like him.
446:
Could we wait until tomorrow?
It is New Year, and they did try, in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city. It's unlikely
Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but don't take a step
outside the dacha! We forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply, addressed to him.
450:
- You'll come for lunch on the first? Promise?
- We promise!
451:
What a shame. Such a nice woman,
and her father's a fence.
452:
Why are you making such a racket?
Who gave you permission to go out?
- He's back... That bad person.
454:
The New Year is here. I hope
this year brings each of you a new beginning.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... Just a moment...
- Where's he going?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of him anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of? He says
he'll find us anywhere and slit our throats.
461:
They say he took a razor to Pockmark's
throat. One slice, and goodbye.
- The jackal's gone completely savage.
462:
Who's come to call? Father Frost!
He's brought presents for you all!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come on. Wear these at home. They're slippers.
464:
- What do I need them for? I don't have a home.
- You will. You've got your whole life ahead of you.
465:
- Meanwhile, they'll come in handy in prison.
- That's all you ever do: predict doom.
466:
This is for you, Vasya...
Gavrila Petrovich, this is yours.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
469: Sour stuff. It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit together
and have a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I'm not having
a heart-to-heart with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! Think I'd play cards
with you, sucker? You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
you take the last letter, W:
"Warsaw." Then you say a city beginning with W.
477: Your turn, Fedya. A city beginning with W.
478:
Workuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Fine. Now you need a city beginning with A.
- Dzhambul. - What's Dzhambul got to do with it?
480:
It's warm there. My home is there.
My mother is there.
481:
Let's try another game. I'll go outside,
you hide something, and I'll come find it.
482:
- You'd be better off finding our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We're hiding something while he peeks
through a hole?
- Then you go out and hide it.
484:
You make sure I don't peek.
- Why me? It's always Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your trap, you little rat!
- Your trap, your trap...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- You came on your own.
- Ah, you're here too.
491:
I went to your place,
but I sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Just walk.
495:
- Sorry to have called you out for nothing, Doctor.
- Not at all.
496:
Give him valerian, warm tea,
and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, hello. We found out
you're in prison,
500:
and we're very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
Which bastard told that kid
his father's in prison?
502:
"Mom was happy too. When your letter
arrived, she cried all day,
503:
and before that, she'd told me
you were a test pilot."
504: A test pilot who raids houses...
505:
"But I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506: you're a good person, just weak-willed."
507:
That's right! So weak-willed he stole
our money and blamed the cabbie.
508:
Get lost! I'll knock your block off,
you rotten radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed? You're forty.
Half your lives are already over.
511:
What's behind you? What do you have now?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, nothing human at all!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we've got to leave.
That doctor will tell the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I, uh, took a razor to her throat...
515: She's in the well. Go and look.
516:
How long was my sentence?
One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten
and the apartment? Say ten!
519:
- What's that add up to?
- Fourteen.
520:
And for a lousy fourteen years,
I'm supposed to put up with this snake?
521:
The one who put that old woman in the well?
Do what you want. I'm going to the police.
523:
What about you? Are you going
to put up with him until you die?
524:
Vasya, I told him earlier
I had a cold, and he...
525:
Enough about your cold already.
Come here...
527:
- What's going on?
- We're cleaning the carpet.
528:
Listen, comrades. The show's over.
First, I'm taking this off.
530:
Once I've done my time, that's it.
I'll go straight and get a job.
531:
- Doing what? Night watchman
at the collective farm back home.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could shovel snow, lay bricks,
or be a translator. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the helmet back!
Who's Docent? A crook.
534:
- Plenty of crooks, but only one helmet.
- They'd have shortened our sentences for it.
535:
Where did he put it?
I think we searched everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was, "I'll rip your trap!"
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
He said, "I'll fish. You dive."
539:
- Wait. What exactly did he say
about fishing? - "I'm fishing
through a hole in the ice.
540:
Can you swim, Squint?" he said.
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole!
541:
That's it! I remember now, the rotten man!
It's in that ice hole in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you oaf?
You could've left a note before hanging yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- Leave him for them. I'm not carrying
a beast his size. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's at the bottom. We have to dive.
546:
Why me? It's always Squint!
Vasya, tell him to go in himself.
547:
I can't! It's cold.
I'll get sick.
548:
- Just now he wanted to hang himself,
and now he's afraid of a cold!
- Sporting greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd kill you both, but I haven't got time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And another one back at the dacha.
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
